    several packages too; at about 16:40, among the review's options, one package plus Templates was
    chosen. The review's ground for it. What the split gives, the areas, their layers and the norm's
    test, comes of the projects and not of the packages; a game names 3DEngine alone and no one
    takes a part; fifteen ids are fifteen uploads and listings a publish, five of them 38 minutes
    behind on 2026-11-10 and a half-listed version failing a restore before; and the whole package
    is under 5 MB, so nothing asks a package of binaries. So the areas stay projects, one 3DEngine
    package carries every area's assembly and the natives, 3DEngine.Templates stays apart as dotnet
    new asks, and the thirteen area ids get no further version, the owner unlisting them. Decision
    85's packages at one version, as 235 and the split made them, give way to this. Item 256.

110. **Places far from the origin, the engine draws against the eye and can be told the world
    moved.** Chosen on 2026-11-12 at about 05:40, on the review's question after item 257, among
    positions in doubles throughout, a call for the origin alone, and this, the engine keeping its
    float API, drawing everything against the eye inside, and giving a game a call that moves the
    world's origin by a whole offset with nothing of the light built again. The review's ground.
    What 257 found was no one pass's fault, every vertex, shadow, lookup of a frame before and point
    from the depth standing in world floats, and a rule at the core costs less than a mend a pass,
    with no break of the API where doubles would change every call that takes a place. Item 264 does
    it, and 258's list is its map.

    deferred lighting pass, and keeping the lighting inlined behind caches and workers. Every model
    shader carries the whole lighting today, 1.3 MB of fragment and 12 s of a first compile in the
    voxel game's terrain before its second copy went, and each feature of the light adds to every
    shader. The forward pass stays, the lighting compiled as functions a shader calls and not as a
    copy in each, 255's trial, measured by the compile's time and the frame's; a deferred pass is
    taken up only if that is not enough.

112. **The lighting's kernels written once.** Chosen on 2026-11-12, among this, two copies with a
    check of their parity, and one engine's lighting alone. The kernels of the radiance cascades
    stand twice, here and in the sibling, ported by hand, and two faults of one night were found and
    mended in both. They go into the RadianceCascades module, written once in Slang, each engine
    giving its own bindings, so a mend lands in both. Item 265 here and the sibling's item 138.

113. **The order of the three.** Decided on 2026-11-12, they are taken after the dither's grain and
    the blobs in the distance, the two things in view, and the publish, and not beside them nor
    parked. Then 264, the places, then 265, the kernels written once, then 255's trial for 111.

114. **An editor as a module both engines use, later.** The direction of 2026-11-12 is that the
    editor is no focus yet and will be. The aim is a full framework in which ImGui frames for editor
    tools are built easily, with helpers that show data such as the ECS and assets in diagnostics
    windows and a way for a shell to have a surface for an editor layout, a module used by both
    engines, made in ImGui as the sibling's is, giving an engine the functions to build an editor on
    or a way to show its data in one. It is thought through further before it is taken up, so no
    item is made and nothing is built. It refines the split's "no editor", none inside the engine
    and one beside both. Until then the two engines stay on one ImGui binding at one version, and
    the engine's ImGui area and its console stay as they are. Added the same morning, of how it sits
    and of what there is. The editor module provides functions and drawing calls that the engine
    uses in its own ImGui scope, in the same process and as ImGui calls alone. So the engine hosts,
    the module owning no window, no ImGui context and no process. The sibling's editor is not taken
    as the module's design; it is progress to learn from, and the module's own design is set out
    when the module is taken up.

Item 264, what three stages do each frame since `a0af50a3` that they did not before, read from the
code ahead of the mend the game's costs ask for.
- `prepare.ImmediateUploadPrepare`. After copying the draw list's vertices and indices into the
  frame's dynamic buffer, as it always did, `ImmediateRenderer.Place` (ImmediateNode.cs 120 to 141)
  looks up the eye of every batch, allocates a flag for every vertex, and for every index of every
  batch drawn through a noted camera reads the vertex back out of the buffer it was written to,
  takes its position against the origin in doubles and writes it again. The buffer is the dynamic
  allocator's, mapped for good in memory the GPU reads, which a driver may give pages that are
  written in order and read back slowly; the copy only writes. That reading back is the likely
  part of 0.015 ms becoming 2.8 to 3.5, which the mend's own reading says. It does all this in
  every frame, whether the origin stepped or not.
- `cpu.model_batches`. Since `3405714a` the instances are written to the mapped instance ring as
  before and then read back out of it in a second pass and written again against the origin
  (ModelRenderer.Instances.cs 169 to 171), the same reading back of mapped memory, every instance
  every frame; and each draw's world matrix is taken against the origin whole, in doubles, for its
  block's box (line 139), where the box took the matrix as it was.
- `cpu.hdr_scene`. Each push of a view works the view against the origin from its eye in doubles
  again (`RenderOrigin.Push` through `Seen`, ModelRenderer.Instances.cs 201 to 206), with a lookup of
  the eye by the view-projection, for every batch of every pass, where the push was the matrix as it
  was; the scene field's stamps and info take their places against the origin in doubles each
  frame likewise, which the field's figures in flight follow.
The mend writes each place against the origin as it is first written, never reading mapped memory
back: the immediate vertices are recorded against an anchor at the camera's eye as they are made,
which is finding 1's mend too and leaves the upload nothing to do while the origin is the anchor;
the instances are taken against the origin as they are written into the ring; and a view's push is
worked once a frame. Its test counts the vertices and instances placed by reading back and the
views worked in a still frame, on the CPU, and holds them at nothing.

Item 264, part 9, its first commit, the views that went un-noted and the lighting's world numbers,
findings 2, 4, 7, 8 and 13 of the review's read.
- The mirrored view (2). `MirrorPlane.Mirrored` makes from the window's noted eye and turn a
  mirrored camera of its own, the eye mirrored in the plane in doubles and the turn mirrored in the
  plane through the world's origin, its near plane the plane laid against the mirrored eye, and the
  frame notes it, so the mirrored pass is pushed from its eye against the origin as the window's
  is, where it went through `Taking` of a view in world floats.
- The probes' gather (8). The capture keeps each face's view-projection made with the eye at
  nothing beside the one it draws through, notes each face by the probe's middle, and the filter
  gathers through the turns alone, `probe_gather.slang` reading a way through a face where it
  added the way to the probe's world middle.

Item 264, the cost of the immediate upload, the model pass's instances and its pushes, mended.
Each place the frame writes into mapped memory is taken against the origin as it is first written,
and that memory is never read back.
- The immediate pass records each run of shapes against an anchor, the eye of the 3D camera it is
  drawn through rounded as the frame's origin is (`DrawList.SetAnchor`, set by `BeginMode3D`), while
  the transform is that camera's, so the sky's pictures drawn through a transform of their own keep
  their space, and a run drawn with a program's shader keeps world numbers, as its shader reads them.
  A point a program gives is taken against the anchor in doubles as it is recorded; a box, a sphere,
  a cylinder, a capsule, a plane, a circle, a billboard, a model's wires and a bounding box are built
  about their middle taken against the anchor with their offsets along the model transform's axes
  (`DrawList.At`, `DrawList.Way`), which is the review's finding 1 mended, a corner far out never a
  float of the world's size. The upload copies the vertices as they are, and each run is drawn
  through its camera against its own anchor from its eye, worked once at the upload; the frame's
  origin moving changes nothing recorded, so its step costs nothing there.
- The model pass writes each instance against the origin as it goes into the ring, a group's
  copies with a packed mesh's scale folded in as they go, where it wrote them and read the whole ring
  back to take them against the origin and the packed groups back again to scale them; and it works
  each view's push and each view against the origin once a frame.
- The moving instances' velocity is written placed and folded as it goes in, where it was copied
  and read back twice.

Item 264, part 9b, the rest of the independent read, the write-only type for mapped memory and the
scene's cost the game's table names.

The write-only type. The maps the uploads write through, `IGraphicsDevice.Map` and
`DynamicBufferAllocator.Map`, hand out a `WriteOnlySpan`, a ref struct over the mapped bytes with a
setter, a slice, a cast, a value written, a copy into, a clear and a fill and no member that reads,
and the readbacks have `IGraphicsDevice.Read`, which reads. Every call site took the type as it
stood, each a write already, but two. The reference tracer's lights were copied into the map and
their places read back out of it to be taken against the origin, now worked in an array and copied
in whole. The ring's copy on several threads made a pointer of the mapped span, which each thread
now maps for itself. WriteOnlySpanTests reads the type's members and finds none that hands the
memory back, where the same reading of a span finds the indexer's getter, ToArray, CopyTo, the
enumerator and the conversion; reads that the maps the uploads take return it and the readbacks'
map a span that reads; and writes through each member and reads what lands.

The findings, each with a test that fails without its mend.
- 11, stereo eyes never noted, holds. Each eye's view-projection is noted with the camera's place and
  its view with that place at nothing, the eye's offset taken with the camera's turn
  (`BeginStereo`), so both eyes are pushed from there. NotedEyeTests reads both eyes' views 71,680
  and 1,140,736 out as at the world's origin within 1e-5; without the notes they are 0.0012 and
  0.022 off.
- 12, transforms not noted, holds for the paths named. A projection set through rlgl inside the
  camera's 3D notes the eye and anchors the shapes after it (`SetRlProjection`); NotedEyeTests reads
  a cube under `rlSetMatrixProjection` far out recorded and pushed as at the origin, which without
  the note was recorded in world floats. The modeling window's outlines note the camera's eye and are
  recorded against it with the mesh's place a move of their own, so the millimeter they are lifted by
  is kept, the anchor the frame had put back after; ModelingWindowTests reads the six faces' outlines
  far out as at the origin, which without the mend failed at both places. The bounce view's probes are drawn through the
  window's camera from its eye (`BounceViewRenderer.ProbesThrough`), WindowViewTests reading it far
  out as at the origin, which `Taking` failed. Shapes inside `BeginShaderMode` in 3D keep world
  numbers, below.
- 13, the lights' signature, was mended in 9a.
- 14, shadow casters ranked through world-number cameras, holds. The views are taken against the
  origin from their eyes with their eyes against it (`LightingUboPrepare.PlacedViews`), as the fit
  had them, and each light's place against it in doubles (`Rank`); ShadowLayoutTests reads the
  window's camera far out as at the origin and eight lamps ranked alike, which failed on the eye.
- 15, `GetRayCollisionMesh`, holds. The ray is taken into the mesh's space, its place less the
  translation turned back, and the distance, point and normal worked back out, a mirroring transform
  keeping its normal's way; Collision3DTests meets a cube 0.3 across five units off at 4.85 far out
  as at the origin, where the world's corners gave 4.8496 at 71,680 and 4.84375 at 1,140,736.
- 16, glow boxes in world floats, holds. The boxes are moved by each world matrix with its
  translation against the origin (`GlowLights.Gather`), each light keeping its middle from the world
  matrices as they are (`Light.Key`), which the places a light keeps from frame to frame and the
  lights' signature read, so an origin's step moves no light's place and begins no cycle, and the
  middles as gathered are placed where the lights are placed (`GlowPlaces.Placed`). GlowLightsTests
  carries a lamp 0.3 wide and two pieces stacked far out as at the origin, sizes and middles, and
  the lights placed alike; the boxes in world floats were 0.002 off in size at 71,680 and 0.031 at

- 17, the same camera's fallback, holds latent. Where no eye was noted, the eyes must be the same too;

- Smaller items. The picking's sphere about a mesh is tested from the ray's place less the mesh's

- 5 and 6 are told in the guide, the camera helpers keeping the look as a target point, which far

The scene's cost. What the scene pass and the window's depth paid each draw since the origin, read
on a probe built as the game's sections are, 660 mesh entities each of a mesh of its own and a
program's shader that keeps its positions, solid and cut-out parts by turns, under the sun's
cascades and a water's mirror, 71,680 out; with the positions not kept, the batches carry no blocks
and the probe read 6.2.60's figures. Each batch's nearest-first order looked its view up by its
hashed view-projection (`Nearest`), and each pass pushed its view at every pipeline it bound, 80
bytes to both stages where 6.2.60 pushed 64 to the vertex stage, so the cascades, binding solid and
cut-out by turns, pushed at every batch, 66 pushes a frame for sixteen cubes. The views and pushes
are kept with the last asked for beside them (`ViewMemo`), so a batch through the view before it
finds it by comparing the matrices, and a view is pushed once a pass, since every pipeline of the
model passes takes the push in one range, which Vulkan keeps set across the pipelines bound after
it; the validation layer reports nothing. ViewMemoTests asks a view and its push 660 times and finds
each looked for once, where each was looked for 660 times; ModelOrderTests reads sixteen cubes under
a sun pushed fewer than sixteen times, 66 without the mend, and a frame of 48 mesh entities of the
game's kind pushing and finding its views as often as one of 16.
